_comment: The 7-id hand-curated pilot, migrated from geBibleApp/docs/REVIEW-pd-both-poles-packet.md as the curation store's seed fixtures. verify_state=human, verbatim_verified=false (packet notes transcriptions are pending a final character-for-character pass). Many quotes are NOT from the seven sweepable voices (Barnes, Ellicott, Pulpit Commentary, Augustine, Plummer, Haley on reconcile; Strauss, Paine on discrepancy) — those carry source_code=null and full_note_ref=null because they cannot be re-verified against verse_commentaries. They are preserved here as the human baseline the machine pass is measured against and as the hand-sourced discrepancy content the sweep cannot reproduce (Decision B).

discrepancy.empty_note: No major public-domain critic presses this as a contradiction — and the leading 19th-c. skeptic, D. F. Strauss, calls the agreement "certainly striking" and reconciles the numbers himself.

excerpts.author: Albert Barnes
excerpts.attribution: Albert Barnes (d. 1870), Notes on the Bible
excerpts.excerpt_text: There can be little doubt that angelic beings are intended here… the whole account relates to the formation of this world, and not of the stars.

excerpts.author: Adam Clarke
excerpts.excerpt_text: This must refer to some intelligent beings who existed before the creation of the visible heavens and earth… the angelic host is meant.

excerpts.author: Charles Ellicott
excerpts.attribution: Charles Ellicott (d. 1905), Commentary for English Readers
excerpts.excerpt_text: by the stars are meant the angels entrusted with their guardianship.

excerpts.author: Keil & Delitzsch
excerpts.attribution: Keil & Delitzsch (Delitzsch d. 1890), Biblical Commentary on the OT
excerpts.excerpt_text: They are actual stars… the fulness of light, in which the morning stars shone forth all together at the founding of the earth, may symbolize one grandly harmonious song of joy.

excerpts.author: The Pulpit Commentary
excerpts.excerpt_text: The stars generally, or the actual stars visible on the morn of creation, are probably meant… Their priority to the earth is implied, since they witness its birth.

excerpts.author: Keil & Delitzsch
excerpts.excerpt_text: The first thing created by the divine Word was "light," the elementary light, or light-material, in distinction from the "lights," or light-bearers, bodies of light, as the sun, moon, and stars, created on the fourth day, are called.

excerpts.author: John Gill
excerpts.excerpt_text: others more rightly take it to be different from the sun, and a more glimmering light, which afterwards was gathered into and perfected in the body of the sun.

excerpts.author: Thomas Paine
excerpts.attribution: Thomas Paine (d. 1809), The Age of Reason, Part II
excerpts.excerpt_text: They make there to have been three days and three nights, evenings and mornings, before there was a sun; when it is the presence or absence of the sun that is the cause of day and night, and what is called his rising and setting that of morning and evening.

excerpts.author: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown
excerpts.excerpt_text: …including the day on which this was spoken and that of the Transfiguration. Matthew and Mark say "after six days," excluding these two days.

excerpts.author: John Gill
excerpts.excerpt_text: Luke takes in the day in which he delivered these sayings, and that in which he was transfigured, and they only reckon the intermediate days.

excerpts.author: Augustine
excerpts.attribution: Augustine (d. 430), Harmony of the Gospels II.xx (NPNF transl., 1888)
excerpts.excerpt_text: …an approach on the part of the centurion to the Lord, which was effected in the person of others, to have chosen to express the matter in this compendious method, There came a centurion unto Him.

excerpts.author: D. F. Strauss
excerpts.work: The Life of Jesus Critically Examined
excerpts.attribution: D. F. Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined (Eliot transl., 1846), §98
excerpts.excerpt_text: …all which according to Matthew the centurion does in his own person, is in Luke done by messengers… this effort to explain the contradictions between the three narratives in a favourable manner is altogether vain.

excerpts.author: Alfred Plummer
excerpts.attribution: Alfred Plummer (d. 1926), Cambridge Bible, on John 18:13
excerpts.excerpt_text: This examination before Annas is given us by S. John only, who tacitly corrects the impression that the examination before Caiaphas was the only one.

excerpts.author: D. F. Strauss
excerpts.attribution: D. F. Strauss, Life of Jesus, §128
excerpts.excerpt_text: the synoptists state Jesus to have been led to the high priest… while John represents him as being led in the first instance to Annas… in this irreconcilable divergency…

excerpts.author: John Haley
excerpts.work: An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible
excerpts.attribution: John Haley (d. 1927), An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874)
excerpts.excerpt_text: …no one of the evangelists denies that more women were present than those he mentions by name… Each writer seems, while not denying the presence of other persons, to single out one or more whom, for some reason, he mentions with particularity.

excerpts.author: Thomas Paine
excerpts.attribution: Thomas Paine, The Age of Reason, Part II
excerpts.excerpt_text: Luke says it was Mary Magdalene and Joanna, and Mary the mother of James, and other women… and John states that Mary Magdalene came alone. So well do they agree about their first evidence!

excerpts.author: John Gill
excerpts.excerpt_text: So Christ, when he first went out to be crucified, carried his cross himself, until the Jews, meeting with Simon the Cyrenian, obliged him to bear it after him; that is, one part of it; for still Christ continued to bear a part himself.

excerpts.author: D. F. Strauss
excerpts.attribution: D. F. Strauss, Life of Jesus, §132
excerpts.excerpt_text: …according to the latter Jesus himself carried his cross thither, while the former state that one Simon a Cyrenian bore it in his stead. The commentators indeed, as if a real agreement were assumed as a matter of course, reconcile these statements thus…
